instructions: In a large bowl, stir together 3 tbsp of the olive oil, the oregano, the garlic (grated or minced very fine), 3 tbsp of lemon juice, 1/2 tsp of the salt and the black pepper. Add the chops and turn them until they're coated. Leave them at room temperature for 15 minutes while you do everything else.

Slice the red onion as thin as you can. Transfer it to a bowl with the sumac. Halve the tomato and slice it, then add it to the onion with 1 tsp of olive oil and 1/4 tsp of the salt. Toss and set aside.
Cut the zucchini into batons about 2 inches long and the pepper into 1/2-inch strips. Toss them with 1 tsp of olive oil and a pinch of the remaining salt.

Heat a large heavy skillet or grill pan over high heat for 2 minutes, until it's smoking hot. Add the zucchini and pepper and cook for 2 minutes on each side, until charred in spots. Transfer them to a plate.

Shake the extra marinade off the chops. Place half of them in the pan with space between them, and cook for 2 to 3 minutes on each side. Turn them only once and don't move them around. You're cooking the lamb to 130°F in the middle for medium-rare, so if you have a thermometer, check there. No thermometer? Press the meat: it should feel springy, like the base of your thumb when you touch your thumb to your middle finger. Transfer to a plate, then cook the other half.
Let the chops rest for 3 minutes.
Taste the relish. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve the lamb with the relish and the grilled vegetables.
method_notes: No version found shows a rating, so the lead is South Yorkshire Food's Kuzu Pirzola (lamb cutlets in olive oil, oregano, garlic and lemon, with a red onion and sumac relish and grilled vegetables), the closest to a pan-seared weeknight dish. Its 4 to 6 hour marinade is cut to 15 minutes at room temperature so the dish stays near 30 minutes, which means a lighter flavor than the traditional version. Rebecca Seal's version (thyme, parsley and sumac onions, 2 minutes a side) confirms the quick pan-sear. The pickled pimentos in the lead's relish and the asparagus are left out.
